conventions.convention: Natural-number time indices include zero. Periodic grids have N≥2 nodes indexed modulo N; finite intervals have N+1 nodes, N−1 interior nodes, and N edges. Grid norms carry weight h, and complex inner products are linear in their first entry. The finite-interval edge pairing has the notation defect recorded below.

Advection means u_t+a u_x=0. For a>0, upwind uses j−1 and ν=ak/h; negative speeds use reflected stencils and |a|k/h. Finite-interval upwind prescribes only the left inflow value and computes the right outflow node.

Wave states are real, with Fourier analysis performed on their complexification. Initialization is U¹=U⁰+kV⁰, with V⁰ the discrete initial velocity; homogeneous Dirichlet displacement and velocity have zero endpoints. No initialization convergence order is asserted.
Consistency is the one-step residual divided by k, uniformly on each fixed C⁶ periodic solution with bounded derivatives, under two-sided positive bounds on k/h.
The wave estimate uses 0<ν≤ν₀<1 and displacement/discrete-velocity data. The mean mode is retained; the repeated Nyquist root at ν=1 requires even N.

load_bearing.statement: Defines the periodic, infinite, and finite-interval index sets, difference operators, weighted grid norms, and interior and edge pairings.

The five periodic advection updates are diagonal in the orthogonal Fourier basis, each Fourier vector having squared norm Nh; their factors and squared moduli are the displayed scheme-specific formulas.
⟨u,−Δ_hv⟩_h = ⟨D₊u,D₊v⟩_{e,h} + u₀ conjugate((D₊v)₀) − u_N conjugate((D₋v)_N). On zero-endpoint functions, −Δ_h is self-adjoint and nonnegative.

For 0<ν≤ν₀<1, nonconstant periodic wave roots are distinct and have modulus one, and ‖Uⁿ‖_{2,h}≤(1+ν₀/√(1−ν₀²))‖U⁰‖_{2,h}+t_n‖V⁰‖_{2,h}. At ν=1 and even N, the Nyquist solution is (−1)ⁿ(A+nB), with B=0 exactly when w¹=−w⁰.

Periodic upwind powers contract for 0≤ν≤1; Lax–Friedrichs and Lax–Wendroff powers contract for |ν|≤1. The stated growing-mode conclusions outside these ranges, for downwind, and for centered advection retain the explicit N=2 aliasing exceptions.

A fixed strict subsequential violation ak/h≥1+ε prevents sampled-maximum convergence for the stated compactly supported datum and infinite-grid homogeneous nearest-neighbor family. Independently, the fixed-period centered family N_q=4q, k_q=h_q/(2a) has unbounded finite-time power norms.

For the stated bounded-derivative C⁶ periodic transport solution and two-sided mesh-ratio bounds, upwind, downwind, centered, and Lax–Friedrichs residuals are uniformly O(h), while Lax–Wendroff residuals are uniformly O(h²).

concerns.concern: The finite-interval Definition writes ⟨p,q⟩_{e,h}=h Σ_{j=0}^{N−1}(D₊p)_j conjugate((D₊q)_j), whereas the periodic Definition writes the same right-hand side as ⟨D₊p,D₊q⟩_{e,h}. Consequently the finite-interval pairing is defined on nodal functions as a derivative pairing, but lem-dirichlet-grid-summation-by-parts applies it to edge arrays D₊u,D₊v. Those arrays have only N entries, so applying the defined D₊ again requires an unavailable endpoint entry. Thus its displayed identity and the cross term defining thm-dirichlet-leapfrog-discrete-energy are not well-typed under the supplied Definition. The intended finite edge pairing h Σ p_j conjugate(q_j) makes the subsequent finite-sum arguments work, but that is not the definition currently written.

seams_checked.note: The common-space example accurately retains one Banach space, one norm, consistency, finite-time power bounds, and the DC qualification. It does not infer convergence directly from varying-grid Fourier bounds.

This is a contextual page prerequisite; the assigned claims do not invoke a stationary-iteration theorem. Their power estimates are proved directly using an orthonormal Fourier basis, so they do not replace power boundedness with a general spectral-radius assertion.

The heat-symbol lemma is used in its one-dimensional periodic, unit-diffusivity specialization for the Laplacian eigenvalue and Fourier basis. Neither boundary stability nor heat time-stepping conclusions are imported.

The renewal upwind algorithm cites the uniform-grid supplier and independently specifies its cell grid, birth inflow, absorbing outflow, loss term, and transport-plus-loss CFL. It does not import periodic scalar-advection stability as a renewal-boundary estimate.
